html:
Teouma, on Efate island, is a cemetery of the first settlers of Vanuatu, people of the Lapita culture, used about 3,000 years ago. Found in 2003, it is the oldest cemetery known in the remote Pacific.

Many of the dead were buried without their heads, which were kept and placed in pots or with other burials. The site gave the finest Lapita pots yet found.

DNA from the skeletons, read in 2016, showed that the first settlers had almost no Papuan ancestry: they came from Island Southeast Asia, part of the Austronesian spread. People from the Bismarck Archipelago arrived soon after, which is why today's ni-Vanuatu carry both lines.
